newsitem.title: KENYA: Supermart, industrials lift Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Supermart, industrials lift Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index gained 5.70 points to 3012.67 on Wednesday on an upward movement in prices on key industrial shares and Uchumi Supermarket, brokers and market officials said.
Turnover was boosted by some 100,000 shares of Rea Vipingo Plantations traded at a steady 10.50 and 200,000 shares of Uchumi Supermarket traded at 45 from 44 on the three-day special lots board.
Turnover was posted at 24.178 million shillings traded on 540,795 shares from 9.325 million shillings traded on 272,824 shares on Tuesday.

On average, prices on key Industrials improved. British American Tobacco traded 80,072 shares at 62.50 from 62, while Firestone East Africa gained 1.0 to 26. Kenya Breweries closed at 50 from 49 while Kenya Power & Lighting Co jumped to 136 from 132.
The sustained increase in price on the power monopoly share continued to intrigue many players in the market.
"We are actually mesmerised by what is happening to that share. In fact, we can't really speculate, it remains to be seen what will happen to it," one broker said.

But brokers agreed that going by it's record in the past, Kenya Power & Lighting Co was expected to make it's company announcements sometime in December and profits were almost guaranteed because of its power distribution monopoly status.
One broker said the index gain reflected a lift in market sentiment: "I think investors are beginning to develop a long-term attitude towards the market," he said.
"If people come into the market now -- I can almost guarantee you that two years down the line they will make almost a 100 percent profit," he added.
Financial analysts in Kenya have previously said that many shares at the Nairobi bourse were undervalued.
CMC Holdings closed at 65 from 63, while Kenya Airways traded 45,586 shares at 8.85 unchanged.
